notes: Two replicas of one shard using ReplicatedMergeTree with ClickHouse Keeper; DDL runs ON CLUSTER. No transactions, no foreign keys; secondary "indexes" are data-skipping (bloom filter) indexes; UPDATE/DELETE are asynchronous mutations.

ddl:
CREATE TABLE customers ON CLUSTER lab_cluster (
  id Int32,
  name String,
  email String,
  country_code String,
  tier String,
  created_at DateTime64(6),
  attrs Nullable(String)
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}') ORDER BY (id)

CREATE TABLE categories ON CLUSTER lab_cluster (
  id Int32,
  parent_id Nullable(Int32),
  name String,
  depth Int32
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}') ORDER BY (id)

CREATE TABLE products ON CLUSTER lab_cluster (
  id Int32,
  category_id Int32,
  sku String,
  name String,
  description String,
  price Decimal(12,2),
  attrs Nullable(String),
  active Bool
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}') ORDER BY (id)

CREATE TABLE orders ON CLUSTER lab_cluster (
  id Int32,
  customer_id Int32,
  status String,
  ordered_at DateTime64(6),
  total_amount Decimal(14,2),
  shipping_country String
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}') ORDER BY (id)

CREATE TABLE order_items ON CLUSTER lab_cluster (
  id Int32,
  order_id Int32,
  product_id Int32,
  qty Int32,
  unit_price Decimal(12,2)
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}') ORDER BY (id)

CREATE TABLE events ON CLUSTER lab_cluster (
  id Int64,
  customer_id Int32,
  event_type String,
  occurred_at DateTime64(6),
  payload Nullable(String),
  value_num Decimal(12,4)
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}') ORDER BY (id)

CREATE TABLE inventory ON CLUSTER lab_cluster (
  product_id Int32,
  warehouse_id Int32,
  qty Int32,
  updated_at DateTime64(6)
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}') ORDER BY (product_id, warehouse_id)
ALTER TABLE products ADD INDEX ix_products_category_id (category_id) TYPE bloom_filter GRANULARITY 4
ALTER TABLE products MATERIALIZE INDEX ix_products_category_id
ALTER TABLE orders ADD INDEX ix_orders_customer_id (customer_id) TYPE bloom_filter GRANULARITY 4
ALTER TABLE orders MATERIALIZE INDEX ix_orders_customer_id
ALTER TABLE order_items ADD INDEX ix_order_items_order_id (order_id) TYPE bloom_filter GRANULARITY 4
ALTER TABLE order_items MATERIALIZE INDEX ix_order_items_order_id
ALTER TABLE order_items ADD INDEX ix_order_items_product_id (product_id) TYPE bloom_filter GRANULARITY 4
ALTER TABLE order_items MATERIALIZE INDEX ix_order_items_product_id
ALTER TABLE events ADD INDEX ix_events_customer_id (customer_id) TYPE bloom_filter GRANULARITY 4
ALTER TABLE events MATERIALIZE INDEX ix_events_customer_id

backup_disk.notes: single-replica backup of every table's parts + metadata into the `backups` disk (/backups); restored under a new database name on the same server

steps.name: prepare
steps.out: Defaulted container "ch1" out of: ch1, wait-keeper (init), init-volumes-init (init)

steps.name: drop old restore db
steps.cmd: DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS lab_restore SYNC

steps.name: RESTORE DATABASE AS lab_restore
steps.cmd: RESTORE DATABASE lab AS lab_restore FROM Disk('backups', 'full')

backup_disk.description: native backup of parts + metadata, restored as a new database

backup_cluster.notes: cluster-coordinated backup (each shard once, the replicas split the parts); drill: DROP TABLE ... ON CLUSTER then RESTORE TABLE ... ON CLUSTER in place

steps.name: BACKUP DATABASE ON CLUSTER
steps.cmd: BACKUP DATABASE lab ON CLUSTER lab_cluster TO Disk('backups', 'cluster')

steps.name: DROP TABLE inventory ON CLUSTER
steps.cmd: DROP TABLE lab.inventory ON CLUSTER lab_cluster SYNC

steps.name: RESTORE TABLE inventory ON CLUSTER
steps.cmd: RESTORE TABLE lab.inventory ON CLUSTER lab_cluster FROM Disk('backups', 'cluster')

pitr.note: table created after the base backup restored from the incremental

incremental.notes: only parts not present in the base backup are written; RESTORE from the incremental resolves the base automatically

steps.name: BACKUP ... base_backup
steps.cmd: BACKUP DATABASE lab TO Disk('backups', 'inc1') SETTINGS base_backup = Disk('backups', 'full')

steps.name: drop old restore db
steps.cmd: DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS lab_restore3 SYNC

steps.name: RESTORE DATABASE AS lab_restore3
steps.cmd: RESTORE DATABASE lab AS lab_restore3 FROM Disk('backups', 'inc1')

incremental.description: incremental on top of the full backup
